FREE BALL 2 of 2 - THE BALL SITS FURTHER FROM THE FOOT WHEN THE PLAYER IS MOVING. WHAT CHANGES: the running and dashing columns of the same first-touch placement table as freeball-touch.json, plus the runDashSetting clamp. Running touch 1.50 -> 1.90 m, dashing touch 2.25 -> 2.70 m, clamp min and max 2.25 -> 2.70 (they are equal in stock and must move together or the clamp swallows the table edit on the one path where it binds). WHO IT AFFECTS: EVERYONE, identically - your stick-controlled player, your AI team-mates and the CPU (match::anime::action::Trap).

EVIDENCE - a-EMULATED, and CORRECTED since the first draft. The chooser 0x14405e130 was re-run under Unicorn from the PRISTINE image sweeping BOTH flags (r9d, and the 5th stack-argument byte which is the BURST flag - proven to be the burst flag because the same byte gates blendStartSpeed.burst at 0x14405e1b4). Metres returned, stock -> this pack:
    gaitOut=Run,  r9d=0, no burst   1.500 -> 1.900
    gaitOut=Run,  r9d=2, no burst   2.250 -> 2.700   (this is where the clamp binds)
    gaitOut=Dash, r9d=0, no burst   2.250 -> 2.700
    gaitOut=Dash, r9d=2, no burst   2.250 -> 2.700
    gaitOut=Run or Dash, TRUE BURST 3.500 -> 3.500   (NO CHANGE)
Every stopping touch is unchanged, which is what keeps this pack separable from freeball-touch.json in a match.

TWO CORRECTIONS THE FIRST DRAFT GOT WRONG, BOTH MATERIAL:
 1. The earlier claim that 'runDashSetting min == max == 2.25 is a HARD PIN on every burst touch, and a large part of why the carried ball feels stuck to the foot' is FALSE. The clamp exists at exactly three sites (0x14405e22c, 0x14405e294, 0x14405e2e7), all inside the gaitOut==Run arm and all guarded by 'cmp esi,2'. It never touches the Dash column and it never runs on a burst. What it genuinely does is bind on ONE cell: gaitOut==Run with r9d==2, where stock clamp(1.5*1.2 = 1.8, 2.25, 2.25) = 2.25 becomes clamp(1.9*1.2 = 2.28, 2.7, 2.7) = 2.7. The min/max edits are still needed for that cell - they are just not the explanation for anything.
 2. A GENUINE BURST TOUCH IS A CODE LITERAL AND THIS PACK CANNOT REACH IT. At 0x14405e321 the chooser discards the table and the clamp entirely and returns a flat 3.5 m (pool cell 0x145ea7a84) whenever the burst byte is set and the player carries on into a run or a dash. Emulated delta from all eight of this pack's edits on that path: +0.000 m, for every gaitIn. If the burst touch is wanted as a lever at all, it is a re-aim of the instruction at 0x14405e321 - a separate exe spec, which has NOT been built.

UNITS ARE METRES, PROVEN BY THE GAME ITSELF: the sibling function 0x14405cc60 prints this same value with Konami's own format string '[trap_dist]offset=%f(m) %s' at 0x146b7bb38.

WHICH CODE PATH WAS MEASURED: 0x14405e130, the shared helper called from 30+ sites. Honest caveat: 0x14405cc60 contains four further inlined copies of the dispatch (0x14405d2b2, 0x14405d44d.., 0x14405d8b7.., 0x14405db9d..) that read the raw table with no clamp and no burst override. b-disassembly only. The direction is the same there.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. It is a LEASH-LENGTH change with NO added variance - each cell is a constant selected by a discrete tuple. Because the 3.5 m burst literal is untouched while the lower cells rise, the overall spread actually NARROWS slightly (stock 0.5-3.5 m, after both free-ball packs 0.8-3.5 m). What is demonstrated is geometry: the ball is knocked further ahead, the player has to run onto it, and a marker has more time and distance to get across. What is NOT ESTABLISHED is any knock-on to kick error - distance-from-foot is not among the named difficulty inputs of the kick-error builder 0x14401a900. Treat this as an INTERCEPTION and tempo lever, not a mis-hit lever. The mis-hit lever is freeball-firsttouch.json.

NOT AVAILABLE AT ALL: the ball corralling BETWEEN touches while dribbling. ballplayer.touch0[] is DEAD (zero readers in the image) and the dribble carry geometry is loaded by match::anime::DribbleMatchingLoder from its own data files, not through ConstantManager. Everything reachable is 'where each touch puts the ball'.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR IN ONE MATCH: a running player pushing the ball ahead of himself rather than dragging it at his ankle, and a late-arriving defender sometimes getting a toe in. THE FAILURE MODE: the ball running away on a routine midfield touch, or touches carrying it out near the touchline - if so, drop 1.9 to 1.75 and 2.7 to 2.45. STRONGER VERSION: 2.3 running and 3.2 dashing.

RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER PACKS ON DISK. This pack and freeball-touch.json are NOT a complete split of freeball-string.json: together they are freeball-string MINUS kickBasis.offsetPos_Idle/Run/Dash and MINUS blendStartAfterFrame, at slightly higher values. kickBasis is a different trap variant with its own readers inside 0x144053700 and stays STOCK at 0.5/1.5/2.0. Other packs writing trap.ballForceDirect: freeball-string.json (all 15), loose-realism-v1/v2.json (kickBasis.offsetPos_Run/Dash), duels-firsttouch.json (rateCollisionSpin). Do NOT stack with freeball-string.json. Verified 2026-09-18 that every field here is live at stock (1.5 / 2.25 / 2.25).

NO DRY-RUN EXISTS for dt270 packs. Verification is tools/tuning_liveness.py check (all 8 fields status 'read', kind float; 5 readers for the offsets, 3 for runDashSetting) plus reading the live values back with gameplay_tune get. APPLY: python tools/gameplay_tune.py apply tools/data/tunings/freeball-carry.json --stack   REVERT: python tools/gameplay_tune.py restore

edits._note: 1.5 -> 1.9 m. Standing, touch into a run. [obj+0x58], read at 0x14405e2dd.
1.5 -> 1.9 m. Running through the touch - by far the most common case in open play. [obj+0x60], read at 0x14405e286.
1.5 -> 1.9 m. Sprinting in, settling into a run. [obj+0x4c], read at 0x14405e21e.
2.25 -> 2.7 m. Standing, touch into a sprint - the knock-and-go. [obj+0x50], read at 0x14405e2d6. The Dash column is never clamped.
2.25 -> 2.7 m. Running, touch into a sprint. [obj+0x64], read at 0x14405e27c. Note the irregular lowercase 'dash' - that is the real field name in the schema.
2.25 -> 2.7 m. Sprinting through the touch. [obj+0x44], read at 0x14405e214.

2.25 -> 2.7 m. Lower clamp, read at [obj+0xc8] by 0x14405e234/0x14405e29c/0x14405e2ef. Binds ONLY on gaitOut==Run with r9d==2 - NOT on bursts, NOT on the Dash column. Must move with max or the Run/r9d==2 cell stays pinned at 2.25.
2.25 -> 2.7 m. Upper clamp, read at [obj+0xc4] by 0x14405e244/0x14405e2ac/0x14405e2ff. Must move with min. min == max is preserved, so the clamp stays well-defined.
